angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 724,224 km at 176.50 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.6659 +/- 0.0174 mas (same row, RUWE 0.88): 176.50 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.041 +/- 0.031 solar radii from Schulte et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1855 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168...32S/abstract): 724,224 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.987 +/- 0.058 solar masses from Schulte et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1855 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168...32S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5359 +/- 89 K from Schulte et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1855 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168...32S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Schulte et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1855 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168...32S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1855.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.397, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
